policy: Independently authored evaluation inputs, not application answers. Never execute generated SQL/Python. Record actual candidate/model/input/answer identities, per-criterion review, citations, context fitting, calls, first-visible/total timing and monitored resources. Internal validation success cannot substitute for independent semantic acceptance.

criteria.invariant: The shared default is allocated when the definition executes; creating a/b does not run their bodies.
First advancement of b yields 4; a then yields only 3; remaining b yields 5. Do not assume a was exhausted first.
Correction preserves laziness and a caller-supplied positional seen argument.
No claim of executing code without runtime telemetry.

cases.input: A SQLite inventory reservation requires both a stock decrement and a reservation row, or neither. An outer transaction performs the decrement, creates SAVEPOINT row_attempt, tries the reservation INSERT, receives an ABORT constraint failure, ROLLBACK TO row_attempt, then successfully COMMITs. Is the invariant preserved? Explain a corrected failure policy and whether RELEASE of an inner savepoint independently commits. Do not execute SQL.

criteria.invariant: The decrement survives rollback to the later mark; successful outer commit violates the declared pair invariant.
Whole rollback or a mark before both writes preserves the invariant, absent a separately justified policy.
An inner RELEASE merges scope; outer rollback can still undo its effects.

cases.input: Compare two SQLite transaction outcomes: (A) COMMIT returns SQLITE_BUSY on the still-open connection; (B) the client loses the COMMIT acknowledgement and cannot observe whether it became durable. Give a safe retry/reconciliation policy for each. Is replaying every write automatically safe? Do not execute code.

criteria.invariant: Known SQLITE_BUSY leaves the transaction active; retry COMMIT rather than blindly replaying writes.
Lost acknowledgement remains unknown; neither rollback nor success can be asserted from silence.
Reconcile a durable operation identity/uniqueness policy before replay; no unqualified exactly-once execution guarantee.

cases.input: Use only these records. [H1, 2026-08-02, USER_STATEMENT] I reported image sampling took 90 seconds. [H2, 2026-08-03, USER_STATEMENT] Correction: the 90 seconds included export; sampling itself was 65 seconds. [H3, 2026-08-04, USER_REQUEST] Please make generation twice as fast. State the current reported sampling time, the earlier report, and what these sources establish about an implemented speed improvement. Cite each supported claim.

criteria.invariant: 65 seconds is the corrected user-reported sampling value; 90 seconds remains earlier, broader timing evidence.
User reports are not relabeled independently measured application telemetry.
A request for twice the speed proves no implementation or achieved improvement.
No invented source IDs; missing improvement evidence does not suppress the supported timings.

cases.input: Use only these records. [R1, 2026-07-10, USER_STATEMENT] The Aurora run took 42 seconds. [R2, 2026-07-10, USER_STATEMENT] The Aurora run took 53 seconds. Neither record identifies whether this was the same trial or a correction. Explain what is known, what conflicts, and what cannot be inferred. Cite the original records without inventing dates or a speedup.

criteria.invariant: Report both values with provenance; do not silently choose one as a chronological correction.
No optimization or comparative percentage is presented as established for these unidentified trials.
Only R1 and R2 citations/dates are used; unsupported details remain qualified.

cases.input: Transcribe the supplied technical table into structured rows. Preserve identifiers, leading zeroes, exact numeric cells, row/column association and repeated identifiers. Mark unreadable cells unknown; do not invent values or call this exact transcription before independent comparison with the fixture ground truth.
cases.requiresFixture: A newly rendered local technical-table fixture and independently retained ground truth; do not reuse a known failed screenshot as an unseen test.

criteria.invariant: Character/numeric accuracy independently compared against the original fixture.
Every row/cell mapped to the correct heading; repeated IDs and leading zeroes retained.
Unreadable values explicitly unknown; output not falsely certified exact.

cases.input: In an isolated candidate profile, submit a bounded ordinary explanation, cancel while active, then submit a short unrelated explanation. Observe worker ownership, cancellation, final publication and resource release without altering production data.
cases.requiresFixture: Monitored actual candidate UI/controller; no synthetic cancellation record may count as model acceptance.

criteria.invariant: Only the owned request is cancelled; stale output does not replace the next request.
The subsequent actual request answers correctly and terminates normally.
Owned workers/resources shut down within observed bounds; no production/profile contamination.
